title: Krassin's Nr 451 and Lutowinoff's Nr 523, Soviet figure radiograms Berlin to Moscow, 1921 (NARA M316 roll 43, from catalogue 669): table recovered by Harumi-Matsuba

documents.shelfmark: NARA RG 59, 861.00, microfilm M316 roll 43 (NAID 604704577), frames 0427-0428

transcription.source: the contributor's transcription from the NARA catalogue OCR, one digit corrected from the image; a blind second transcription of the images by OpenAI Codex agrees on 1,598 of 1,600 digits (his figure); the project did not see the images and no human has checked
transcription.notes: Five-digit groups, 1,600 digits = 40 x 40; the clear heading names Krassin to Tschitscherin, the indicator word SOROK (40); the catchword /21545/ at the head of frame 0428 is left out; digit 182 is overstruck (kept as 5).

documents.shelfmark: NARA RG 59, 861.00, microfilm M316 roll 43 (NAID 604704577), frame 0432

transcription.source: the contributor's transcription from the NARA catalogue OCR; a blind second transcription by OpenAI Codex agrees on 575 of 575 digits (his figure); the project did not see the images and no human has checked
transcription.notes: 575 digits, one short of 24 x 24; the clear heading names Lutowinoff to Tschitscherin for Litvinov with copies to Chicherin, Molotov and Shlyapnikov, indicator words DWADZAT TCHETYRE (24); a stray '60' typed between lines 9 and 10 is not included.

system.summary: Each Russian letter becomes a digit pair from a 5 x 6 table (first digit 6-9 or 0, second 0-5), the pairs are written row by row into an N x N digit square (N spelled out before the groups) and sent column by column.

prior_solution.where: None found by the contributor on 10 Nov 2026 (this ledger, its issues, GitHub, Cryptiana, Tiltman, Chernoperov, web search); the Soviet document editions (Sovetsko-germanskie otnosheniya vol. 2, DVP SSSR IV), TNA HW 12 and NARA RG 457 were not read and may hold the text.

conditions.human_role: Harumi-Matsuba directed the work and decided on publication; Anthropic Claude (Claude Fable 5.2) found the system, recovered the table, made the reading and the documents; OpenAI Codex transcribed the images blind as a second reader and, with Claude Sonnet, judged sampled digits. No human compared the images with the transcription. The project re-ran the decryption with its own code; it has not seen the images.

solution.what: Contributor: five-digit groups taken from the NARA catalogue OCR of M316 roll 43, I turned into 1, the catchword on frame 0428 dropped, one digit changed from the image; a blind second transcription of eight image strips by OpenAI Codex agrees on 1,598/1,600 and 575/575 digits.

Contributor: digit counts match the number word (1,600 = 40 x 40, 575 about 24 x 24); cut into runs of N, columns of high digits alternate with columns of low digits (94.9% and 95.1% of non-zero digits); paired columns give about 30 pair types with IC 0.0551 and 0.0490.

Contributor: digit pairs written row by row into an N x N square and sent by columns, columns not permuted (long repeats recur at different row positions); rows right to left in Nr 451 (text ends at the right edge before the 00 filler), mirror layout in Nr 523.

Contributor: simulated annealing on the 764 pairs of Nr 451 alone, assigning Russian letters to the 32 commonest pairs, scored with Russian letter 4-grams, no crib; three runs reached the same score and the text read; three values (10, 33, 71) were then corrected on reading and 28 taken out.
Contributor: the table from Nr 451, unchanged, applied to Nr 523, which was not used to build it: 279 of 288 pairs read as sense.

Contributor: 1,000 shuffles of the table's letter values; none reaches the real table's mean 4-gram score in either message (real -11.127 / -12.329, best shuffled -14.686 / -14.796); the same table with rows read the other way scores -13.889 / -14.282.

Contributor: this ledger, its issues and pull requests, GitHub code search, Cryptiana, wenmi, Tiltman's Experiences 1920-1939, Chernoperov's article on Kopp, web searches in Russian and English: no decipherment or plaintext found; the Soviet document editions were not read.

Project check: an own decoder written from the issue's description (verify.py) gives both texts identical pair for pair to the contributor's reading files; the Russian read through as sentences. NARA images not reachable from the project; docs/_validate.py has no Russian model.

Read share recounted over cipher words only (README Conventions, 16 Nov 2026), holes by words, sure words only, a letter corrected in a rebuilt key a hole. Both messages are wholly cipher. By hand on the contributor's word breaks in translation.md: Nr 451 95 of 109 words read (87.2%), 14 holes (seven words on the off-table pairs 28 x3, 77 x2, 91 and 14, and seven with a wrong, empty or unknown letter); Nr 523 41 of 47 (87.2%), 6 holes (numbers 16 and 76 53 18, four words with a wrong letter). Both under the 95% bar, so read in part; the earlier 0.982 and 0.969 counted digit pairs. translation.md carries both messages and the English, so v10_relabel.py (0.913, not split) cannot reproduce the figure.

outcome.method_basis: Contributor's method: the table was recovered by annealing on the ciphertext of Nr 451 alone with no crib, and confirmed on Nr 523; the project re-ran the decryption with its own code but did not repeat the search or see the images.

validation.notes: no Russian model in lang/; the contributor's 1,000-shuffle control and the reading of Nr 523, not used to build the table, stand in for it

texts.label: Nr 451, Krassin to Chicherin, Berlin to Moscow, 30 May 1921
texts.summary: Krasin reports that the Berlin trade representation now works well, that the auditing commission has found damaging material on its previous period, asks for Kulyabko to be sent to Berlin and for no decisions to be taken before the commission reports.

reading_review.note: Read the decryption as Russian sentences with the contributor's word breaks: telegraphic but coherent throughout; holes are the off-table pairs (комисс, раб) and seven single wrong letters, none blocking the sense.

texts.note: 16 Nov 2026, cipher words only: 95 of 109 words read (87.2%), counting as holes the off-table pairs, the numbers and the words with a wrong or empty letter (before 0.982, counted over digit pairs). The message is wholly cipher, so nothing was split. Counted by hand on the contributor's word breaks in translation.md; v10_relabel.py cannot reproduce it, because translation.md also holds the other message and the English.

texts.label: Nr 523, Lutovinov to Chicherin for Litvinov, Berlin to Moscow, 14 June 1921
texts.summary: Lutovinov protests against Kopp being kept in Berlin as polpred before the audit ends, asks to whom he should hand over his duties and says he will hand over to Brodovsky within hours.

reading_review.note: Read the decryption as Russian sentences: coherent throughout; two numbers unread and four single wrong letters of a 4/5 confusion shape.

texts.note: 16 Nov 2026, cipher words only: 41 of 47 words read (87.2%), counting as holes the off-table pairs, the numbers and the words with a wrong or empty letter (before 0.969, counted over digit pairs).
